title: DA: Adequate pork supply until Q1 2027
summary: The Department of Agriculture has given assurance that domestic pork stocks remain adequate to meet demand until the first quarter of 2027 despite concerns that a 60-day import ban could lead to a…

blocks.text: Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said the country has enough locally produced and imported pork to meet consumer demand.

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Agriculture (DA) has given assurance that domestic pork stocks remain adequate to meet demand until the first quarter of 2027 despite concerns that a 60-day import ban could lead to a supply shortage.

“The local industry stated that we have a lot of pork, and the data of the DA shows that we have a lot of local pork. We also have a lot of imported pork, so I think we won’t run out,” Tiu Laurel told reporters.
Earlier, a US Department of Agriculture (USDA) report warned of a potential pork shortage in the Philippines by the first quarter of 2027 due to the government’s two-month ban on imported pork.
The report noted that domestic production in the first three months of next year would have to increase by at least 14 percent to meet demand under a scenario involving reduced imports.
The Philippines consumed 430,000 metric tons of pork in carcass weight equivalent in the first quarter of 2026, according to the USDA.
The DA ordered a 60-day ban on pork imports after finding that surging foreign pork imports had caused serious injury to the country’s hog industry under Department Order 33.
The order is expected to take effect on Nov. 26.
Meanwhile, Tiu Laurel said meat processors had asked to be exempted from the import ban. He said he would meet with them on Nov. 24 to hear their concerns and assess their inventory.
“The processors have a request if they can be considered exempt from the 60-day ban. So, we’ll talk to the processors tomorrow to hear out. We’ll audit their stock levels,” he said.
Tiu Laurel added that representatives from the local hog industry would also attend the meeting, with the DA serving as mediator.
